skill.name: spec-workflow
skill.description: Guides implementation work through a spec-driven workflow. It requires acceptance criteria review, TDD steps, scope checks, and completion validation before handoff.
skill.summary: Apply a spec-driven TDD workflow for acceptance-criteria based implementation.
skill.author: Clionegohan

security_audit.summary: Most backtick-related findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline formatting, and TypeScript examples. The filesystem findings are confirmed because SKILL.md references hidden .ai files through parent-directory traversal at lines 306-307.

remediation.suggestion: Move the referenced workflow documents into the skill package or require explicit user approval before reading parent paths.
State that /branch and /pr steps require explicit user approval before any repository branch or pull request action.
Use plain prose for non-code workflow examples where possible to reduce false shell-execution alerts.

content.value_statement: Feature work often drifts beyond approved acceptance criteria. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through AC review, TDD, scope checks, and completion review.
actual_capabilities: Prompts for acceptance criteria confirmation before implementation starts.
Maps EARS-style acceptance criteria into test planning steps.
Guides Red, Green, and Refactor phases during implementation.
Identifies requests that are outside the current subtask scope.
Supports branch and pull request handoff after user confirmation.
limitations: Requires existing subtask specifications in the expected specs folder structure.
Does not create upstream epics, stories, or acceptance criteria.
Depends on project test tools that already exist in the workspace.
Branch and pull request steps depend on separate workflow skills.

use_cases.title: Implement Approved Subtasks
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to read a subtask, confirm acceptance criteria, and implement only the approved scope.

use_cases.title: Keep Delivery Aligned
use_cases.description: Use acceptance criteria checks to prevent extra features and confirm completion before status updates.

use_cases.title: Structure AI Pair Programming
use_cases.description: Guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a repeatable TDD cycle for feature work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Subtask
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single approved implementation task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement subtask 001-01-01. Read the matching spec, summarize the acceptance criteria, and ask for approval before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Tests from Criteria
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert acceptance criteria into a test-first implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the spec workflow for this story. Derive test cases from each acceptance criterion before making implementation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Scope Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a request that may not belong in the active subtask.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this requested change is inside the current subtask acceptance criteria. If it is outside scope, propose the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Story Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after implementation and verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: After all tests pass, check every acceptance criterion, update the subtask status, and prepare the branch and pull request handoff.

output_examples.input: Implement the user authentication subtask from the current spec.
output: Summarizes the user story and acceptance criteria.
Asks for approval before implementation starts.
Plans failing tests, minimal implementation, and refactor checks.
Reports completion against each acceptance criterion.

output_examples.input: Also add CI setup while working on the configuration subtask.
output: Identifies CI setup as outside the current acceptance criteria.
Explains why it should not be added to the current subtask.
Offers to define it as a separate follow-up task.

output_examples.input: Finish this story and prepare review handoff.
output: Checks that all subtasks and tests are complete.
Requests confirmation before branch or pull request actions.

best_practices: Keep each prompt tied to one subtask and one approved acceptance criteria set.
Review the proposed tests before allowing implementation changes.
Require explicit approval before branch, status, or pull request updates.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to invent acceptance criteria without upstream specification work.
Do not bundle unrelated feature requests into one subtask implementation.
Do not skip the Red phase when tests are available for the project.

faq.question: Does this skill create specifications?
faq.answer: No. It assumes epics, stories, subtasks, and acceptance criteria already exist.

faq.question: Can it work without tests?
faq.answer: It can plan the workflow, but the TDD cycle depends on project test tooling.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: It guides implementation steps and asks for approval before key workflow actions.

faq.question: What specification format does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a three-level epic, story, and subtask structure under a specs folder.

faq.question: Can it handle EARS acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to map EARS statements into test planning steps.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large stories?
faq.answer: It works best when large stories are split into small subtasks with clear acceptance criteria.
